::: {.callout-note}
**Simulated data · fictional compound.** FJF-2026 does not exist. Every number in this report is generated by code. The tables and figures are those of the pipeline (`docs/sap/fjf-2026-iss-treatment-outputs.yml`), embedded unchanged and double-programmed.
:::

# Plan and status

The analysis follows the plan `docs/sap/fjf-2026-iss-sap.yml`, version `r plan$version`, frozen with the tag `iss-sap-v1.0`. The plan was committed on 2026-11-13, while the unblinded pipeline was still running and before any result with the real arms was read (ADR 0034); the implementation choices the plan leaves open are in ADR 0035. No analysis has been added to the plan, so none is labelled post hoc.

The analyses are descriptive: confidence intervals are not adjusted for multiplicity and no p-value tests a hypothesis.

# Pool and measures

```{r}
#| results: asis
cols <- plan$pools[[1]]$columns
asis(csr_markdown(
  data.frame(Column = vapply(cols, `[[`, "", "label"), From = vapply(cols, `[[`, "", "from")),
  c("Column", "From")
))
```

- **Pool.** `r plan$pools[[1]]$definition`
- **Incidence** is the number of patients with at least one event, n (%). The **exposure-adjusted incidence rate (EAIR)** is the number of patients with at least one event per 100 patient-years of exposure, the measure for comparing columns, because the studies last 12 and 26 weeks and the 20 mg column draws more on the longer study than placebo does. The event rate is events per 100 patient-years.
- FJF-2026 20 mg against placebo is compared with the **Mantel-Haenszel risk difference stratified by study** (variance of Sato), and, for hypoglycaemia of level 2 or 3, with the rate ratio of a **negative binomial** model with treatment and study as factors and the exposure as offset.

# Exposure (I6)

```{r}
#| results: asis
table_md("T-ISS-8")
```

The compliance of the columns that come from FJF-2026-201 is about 186%. It is not a property of the drug: the study takes two tablets a day (double dummy) and its ADaM uses the derivation of FJF-2026-301, which counts one. It does not depend on the arm and no result of this report uses it (ADR 0035). Its correction is the reviewer's decision.

# Hypoglycaemia (I3)

```{r}
#| results: asis
table_md("T-ISS-14")
table_md("T-ISS-15")
```

Episodes of level 2 or 3 are few, so the model cannot estimate the dispersion and is close to a Poisson model; its rate ratio and interval are the same in the independent second programming (ADR 0035).

# Discussion and conclusions

The discussion and the conclusions are written by the study team, that is the reviewer, from the results above. This report states what the tables contain and does not interpret them clinically. Whatever is added beyond the plan must be labelled post hoc.

# Quality

```{r}
#| results: asis
asis(csr_markdown(d$qc, c("Level", "Units", "Compared", "Second programming clean")))
```

The second programming (`qc/iss/tlf_qc.R`) starts from the ADaM datasets of each study, not from the pooled datasets, and fits the negative binomial model by direct likelihood. A difference in any cell stops the pipeline. Both programs have the same author.
